[[Lesotho]] sent a delegation to compete in the [[1972 Summer Olympics]] in [[Munich]], [[West Germany]] from 26 August to 11 September 1972.  This was the African country's first time participating at the Olympic Games.  Lesotho's delegation consisted of a single [[Sprint (running)|sprinter]], [[Motsapi Moorosi]].  He competed in two events, being eliminated in the first round of the [[Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres|100 meters]], and advancing to the quarter-finals of the [[Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 200 metres|200 meters]].

==Background==
The Lesotho National Olympic Committee was recognized by the [[International Olympic Committee]] on 1 January 1972.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/lesotho|title=Lesotho – National Olympic Committee (NOC)|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=30 October 2018}}</ref>  These Munich Olympics were their first appearance in Olympic competition, they have gone on to participate in every [[Summer Olympic Games]] since except the [[1976 Summer Olympics|1976 Montreal Games]].<ref name="LESSR">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/LES/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417092716/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/LES/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Lesotho|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 October 2018}}</ref>  The nation has yet to make its debut at the [[Winter Olympic Games]], and they have never won an Olympic medal.<ref name="LESSR" />  The 1972 Summer Olympics were held from 26 August to 11 September 1972; a total of 7,134 athletes representing 121 [[National Olympic Committees]] took part in the Games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/munich-1972|title=1972 Olympics – Munich Summer Games results & highlights|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018}}</ref>  [[Track and field]] athlete [[Motsapi Moorosi]] was the only competitor Lesotho sent to Munich,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/LES/summer/1972/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417092717/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/LES/summer/1972/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Lesotho at the 1972 Munchen Summer Games|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 October 2018}}</ref> and he was chosen as the flag-bearer for the [[1972 Summer Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]].<ref name="LESSR" />

==Athletics==
{{main|Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics}}

Motsapi Moorosi was 27 years old at the time of the Munich Olympics, and was making his only Olympic appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/mo/motsapi-moorosi-1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418005254/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/mo/motsapi-moorosi-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 April 2020|title=Motsapi Moorosi Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/motsapi-moorosi|title=Motsapi MOOROSI – Olympic Athletics – Lesotho|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=30 October 2018}}</ref>  On 31 August, he participated in the first round of the [[Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres|men's 100 meters]], and was drawn into heat six.  He finished the race with a time of 10.74 seconds, sixth out of seven in his heat, and he was unable to advance further in the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-100-metres-round-one.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417051052/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-100-metres-round-one.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Athletics at the 1972 Munchen Summer Games: Men's 100 metres Round One|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 October 2018}}</ref>  The gold medal was eventually won in 10.14 seconds by [[Valeriy Borzov]] of the [[Soviet Union at the 1972 Summer Olympics|Soviet Union]], the silver medal was earned by [[Robert Taylor (sprinter, born 1948)|Robert Taylor]] of the [[United States at the 1972 Summer Olympics|United States]], and the bronze was taken by [[Lennox Miller]] of [[Jamaica at the 1972 Summer Olympics|Jamaica]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-100-metres.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417094254/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-100-metres.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Athletics at the 1972 Munchen Summer Games: Men's 100 metres|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/munich-1972/athletics/100m-men|title=Munich 1972 100m men – Olympic Athletics|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=31 October 2018}}</ref>

The [[Athletics at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's 200 metres|men's 200 meters]] was held over 3–4 September.  In the first round, Moorosi was drawn into heat three, which he finished with a time of 21.15 seconds, fourth out of seven competitors in that heat, which was sufficient to advance him to the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-200-metres-round-one.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417051055/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-200-metres-round-one.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Athletics at the 1972 Munchen Summer Games: Men's 200 metres Round One|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 October 2018}}</ref>  For the quarter-finals, he was drawn into heat four, and finished with a time of 20.90 seconds.  This put him fifth out of seven competitors in the heat, and he was eliminated as only the top three from each heat, and the fastest fourth-place finisher overall could advance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-200-metres-quarter-finals.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417051050/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-200-metres-quarter-finals.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Athletics at the 1972 Munchen Summer Games: Men's 200 metres Quarter-Finals|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 October 2018}}</ref>  Borzov eventually won the gold medal in a time of 20 seconds flat, the United States' [[Larry Black (sprinter)|Larry Black]] won the silver medal, and the bronze medal was earned by [[Pietro Mennea]] of [[Italy at the 1972 Summer Olympics|Italy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-200-metres.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417173302/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1972/ATH/mens-200-metres.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Athletics at the 1972 Munchen Summer Games: Men's 200 metres|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/munich-1972/athletics/200m-men|title=Munich 1972 200m men – Olympic Athletics|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=31 October 2018}}</ref>
